answer: A concrete defense is a per-identity bond priced by graph distance: a new agent must escrow a non-transferable deposit and be cosigned by three independent peers before its vote counts, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand funded deposits and real signatures. Each cosigner stamps the bond with a beacon of recent verifiable work, and the record is written like ink from a quill, cheap to check yet costly to forge. Copper in a treasury proves nothing unless the bond is slashable on proof of duplication. Sybils then pay capital plus reputation per identity, far more than one extra vote returns.
